correctness.rationale: For finite M, Fourier coefficients of K=H_q(x-y)(1+sum_j a_j cos j(x+y)) factor as D W D with D_nn=q^(n^2/2)>0 and W the multiplication Toeplitz matrix of w(z)=1+sum_j a_j q^(-j^2)cos(2jz). The factorization is exact since ((n+m)/2)^2=(n^2+m^2)/2-j^2 on n-m=±2j. Nonnegative w suffices; if w<0 on an arc, a trigonometric polynomial g has ∫w|g|²<0, and inverse Fourier scaling by nonzero D on its finite support yields a negative quadratic form, proving necessity for all finite sample Gram matrices. If w>=0, its constant coefficient is one, so its finitely many zeros cannot support an analytic nonzero H_sqrt(q)*ν for nonzero finite complex measure; energy strictly >0, giving finite-site strictness and RKHS C(T) universality by Hahn-Banach duality. The two-harmonic piecewise quadratic min over u=cos(2z) follows exactly; an explicit 12-term polynomial gives a negative witness beyond |a1|=q. Independently checked Fourier exponent relation and M=2 candidate minimization; inspected full RESULT.md and rational checker, not relying on finite tests alone.
